units.translation: 749 ⟦1⟧ 'revering you' as in ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧, construed as a negative verb with ⟦4⟧ (not in the passage from the Persians).

⟦1⟧ = ⟦2⟧; ⟦3⟧ shows that ⟦4⟧ too is to be taken gnomically and generally. ⟦5⟧ cannot be satisfactorily explained in any way, neither in that of the scholiast (⟦6⟧), nor in that of G. Hermann, = ⟦7⟧, for that would at least have to be (Dindorf) ⟦8⟧. ⟦9⟧ (aorist like ⟦10⟧) is graphically very close and is a favorite word of the poet (155 ⟦11⟧ etc.); ⟦12⟧ H. Voss, Wecklein. 754–777 Orestes.
the vote is able both to cast and to set upright a house
having cast his judgment in voting
— 756 ⟦1⟧ in Homeric fashion; cf. ⟦2⟧ with Homer Z 462 (Wecklein).
and some one of the Greeks will say

⟦1⟧: cf. ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧. ⟦4⟧; Zeus as the ultimate author has directed everything thus, and just as he comes as the third to the two tutelary gods, so he has also shown himself as ⟦5⟧, just as to him as ⟦6⟧ the third libation is due; cf. ⟦7⟧ (after the ⟦8⟧ and the ⟦9⟧) ⟦10⟧ (also ⟦11⟧). The ⟦12⟧ at 761 shows that the fictitious speech extends no further than ⟦13⟧. ⟦14⟧ stands in the general meaning of 'to have regard for', cf. ⟦15⟧ (92) 151. ⟦16⟧ on 579.
for what is accomplished for mortals without Zeus?
and Zeus the savior as the third
of Zeus, the all-author, the all-worker
